findings.title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `CryptoProvider` is a public extension interface, and making `order()` abstract means implementations compiled against the previous API do not implement the new method. Such providers can fail with `AbstractMethodError` when provider discovery calls `order()`, while source implementations no longer compile. Give the method a default value to preserve compatibility, or otherwise account for existing third-party providers.

findings.title: Providers with equal order are selected according to discovery order
findings.body: The built-in Default, Elytron, and FIPS providers all return order `200`, but this comparator provides no tie-breaker. `ServiceLoader` discovery order depends on classpath/service-file ordering, so when more than one of these providers is present the selected implementation can change with packaging or runtime classpath order. Since the selected provider determines cryptographic and FIPS behavior, equal-priority providers need a deterministic resolution or ambiguity must remain an error.
